purpose: Bazel 9.3 `.ar`/`.deb` extraction (DecompressorValue.java:151-152,172 AR_FORMATS, ArFunction.java over commons-compress 1.26.1 ArArchiveInputStream/ArArchiveEntry/ParsingUtils): type inference by `type=` and by suffix (extract: getDecompressor(type) or the archive basename; download_and_extract: DownloadManager.getDownloadDestination names the file from the first URL's decoded basename + `.TYPE`, FS_UNSAFE_CHARS -> `_`, and the decompressor is chosen by that name only), member names (BSD/plain, GNU `/` terminator, GNU `//` table and `/N` references, BSD `#1/N`, trim, PathFragment normalization, subdirectories, duplicates), ArFunction ignoring strip_prefix and strip_components and applying rename_files, file modes (`mode | 0400`, chmod keeps setuid/setgid/sticky), atime/mtime = the member timestamp (also 0 and negative), lazy output creation by extract vs eager by download_and_extract, module_ctx.extract, @bazel_tools http_archive of a .deb (the rules_distroless deb_import shape), commons-compress's errors for corrupt and truncated archives (silent short data at EOF), and Bazel's filesystem errors (`(File exists)`, `(Is a directory)`, `(Permission denied)`, `Invalid file path`). Motivation: ~/code //src/python/baseimage:image (rules_distroless apt -> deb_import -> http_archive of Debian .deb files) failed with `archive type deb is not supported by the native extractor`.

reference.environment: env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME/TMPDIR private LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8; default registry (bcr.bazel.build) for the module graph only; archives served by a loopback HTTP server (127.0.0.1:<PORT>); one workspace and output base for all cases

normalization: <WS> = the workspace; <REPO> = the repository directory (genuine <OB>/external/+probe+CASE, native <cache>/repositories/direct/stages/<hex>); 127.0.0.1:<PORT>; download temporary directories temp<N>. Listings are printed by the repository rule right after extraction (`find -printf '%P|%y|%m|%T@|%A@|%s'` and sha256sum; directories without times); timestamps from 1750000000 on (the callback's own ctx.file writes and atimes refreshed by reading) are <NOW>.
comparison (tests/ar_archives.rs, live): EXACT: both succeed and the native listing equals the genuine listing. EXACT_LABELS: both succeed and the queried labels are equal after `//`. EXACT_MESSAGE: both fail and genuine's `Error in extract|download_and_extract: ` text is contained in native stderr. EXPECTED_NATIVE_UNSUPPORTED (genuine succeeds) and REFERENCE_CRASH (genuine exits 37) are native failures with the recorded native message. Exit codes: genuine `query` exits 7 for a failed fetch, native 1 (recorded, not compared).
genuine_key_findings: Bazel 9.3 deletes a repository directory before its implementation runs (RepositoryFetchFunction.setupRepoRoot): a GNU symbol table member `/` (empty name) then writes a regular FILE at the repository path and the next member fails with `<repo> (File exists)`; with download_and_extract the output exists first: `<repo>/out (Is a directory)`.
strip_prefix is ignored (no `Prefix ... was given` error), strip_components is ignored, rename_files applies to member names and may create subdirectories.
Modes are `mode | 0400` including setuid/sticky bits (4755, 1644); mtime and atime are the member timestamp (0, -1, +5 parse like Long.parseLong).
A member whose data is cut short by the end of the archive is extracted short without an error; trailing bytes that are not a full header are `Truncated ar archive`.

`Invalid header` prints the 8 bytes as decoded from US-ASCII: control bytes raw, bytes above 0x7F as `?`. A BSD name cut short is `new EOFException()`: the message `null`. NUL bytes in a name are `Invalid file path` (java.io.File).
A member name with bytes above 0x7F crashes Bazel 9.3 (exit 37, IllegalStateException in StringUnsafe.getInternalStringBytes for the U+FFFD commons-compress decodes).
`../escape.txt` is written beside the repository directory (getRelative normalization); native extraction refuses names that leave the destination.

download_and_extract names the archive `<output>/temp<N>/<name>`: `bad+name.deb` -> `bad_name.deb`, type=deb on `bad` -> `bad.deb`, type=ar on `bad+name.deb` -> `bad_name.deb.ar`, type=rar -> `Expected a file with a ... suffix (got .../basic.deb.rar)`; with mirrors the FIRST URL names it (`first%20name.bin` -> `first_name.bin.deb`) even when a later mirror serves it.

def _list(mctx, case, listed):
    r = mctx.execute(["/bin/sh", "-c", LIST, "sh", str(mctx.path(listed))])
    print("AR-LISTING-BEGIN %s\n%sAR-LISTING-END" % (case, r.stdout))

def _ext_impl(mctx):
    mctx.extract(Label("//:basic.deb"), output = "x", rename_files = {"debian-binary": "meta/version"})
    _list(mctx, "module_ctx_extract", "x")
    mctx.extract(Label("//:empty.ar"), output = "e")
    _list(mctx, "module_ctx_empty", "e")
    probe(name = "module_ctx_extract", case = "noop")
    probe(name = "module_ctx_empty", case = "noop")

ext = module_extension(implementation = _ext_impl)
